maya: planning to roll out a canary that targets 5% of traffic but using a session-bucket instead of header-slicing. reason: headers are noisy and QA often injects header overrides which mess with real user sampling. propose: percentage by hash(session_id) mod 100 < pct. simple, sticky, respects user sessions. snippet of the idea:
```yaml
route: /v1/generate
match: { path_prefix: /v1/generate }
canary: 
  variant: model-x-v2
  percentage: 5
  selector: "mod(hash(cookie.session_id), 100)"
  sticky: true
  override_header: x-rw-force-variant  # admin only
```
Thoughts? :eyes:

kevin: +1 on session-based sampling. two quick questions: 1) precedence with header override — do we want admin header to always win? 2) what about anonymous sessions (no cookie)? fall back to ip hash?

maya: yes header admin should always win but only for admin tokens (enforce at auth layer). for no-cookie, fallback to ip hash then to random uuid. keep selector chain predictable.

sam: careful about using IP for prod sampling — proxies and NAT will skew. maybe use client_fingerprint if available, else random. also: we need the gateway to emit a telemetry tag like experiment_id and variant so downstream metrics can be sliced.

nina: telemetry +1. and make sure we don't leak PII in tags. session_id should be hashed before being included in logs/metrics. also need to track quotas per-variant (so canary usage doesn't eat baseline quota).

kevin: agree on hashed ids. for matching logic, we could implement a modular matcher in the gateway runtime. pseudo: 
```js
function inCanary(context, pct, salt) {
  const id = context.cookie.session_id || context.client.fingerprint || context.ip;
  const h = hash64(id + salt) % 100;
  return h < pct;
}
```
That lets us change salt per rollout to reshuffle population if needed.

maya: nice. about console UX: I want a slider to change percentage with an optional burn-in schedule (5% -> 20% -> 50%). also ability to pin a user id into variant for QA and to see per-variant latency/err rates in the rollout dashboard.

sam: rollout windows should be configurable with auto-rollback threshold (e.g., if error_rate increases > 3x baseline or p95 latency degrades > 200ms). console should show those signals and allow one-click rollback.

kevin: implementation detail: routing precedence table must be clear: 1) exact path + admin override header 2) canary selectors (session/ip/fingerprint) 3) header-based experiments (old) 4) default route. document that in API gateway docs. also add a dry-run mode that tags requests with variant but doesn't route them — useful for telemetry validation.

nina: dry-run is critical. we should run dry-run for 24h before any traffic shift. also ensure billing/quotas counting rules: dry-run shouldn't count against variant quota.

maya: on security: explicitly disallow query-param override for variant selection. too easy to leak/share. admin header only + console pin.

kevin: noted. one more: rollout TTL and cleanup. if you change percentage, old salt variations should expire after 7 days to avoid ghost splits. add rotation policy.

sam: operational metrics we need emitted by gateway: experiment_id, variant, sampled:true/false, route_version, model_id, latency_ms, status_code, auth_tier. keep tag keys short. example: `exp:canary_2026_03;var:v2;sample:1`

maya: router-bot: starting canary configuration PR in infra repo, will post link. :shipit:

router-bot: deploy-bot: Created canary-config branch and kicked off CI (build 548). Tests: unit + e2e routing harness.

kevin: when CI passes, let's feature-flag the selector behind `enable_session_canary` and roll it to staging. also add a small load test to verify percent split accuracy under different client distributions.

nina: I'll add telemetry dashboards: per-variant throughput, p50/p95, error ratio, and cost-per-1000-tokens. will link dashboards in the PR description.

sam: and add a convergent test for sticky behavior: user should remain in same variant across cookie rotation within the burn-in window.

maya: awesome. action items: maya -> PR with config + salt support; kevin -> add modular matcher + dry-run; nina -> dashboards + redact hashed ids; sam -> rollback automation rules. we'll do 24h dry-run then 5% canary.

kevin: @maya ping when PR is up, I'll review.
